topic: The Mystery of India's Disappearing Villages
angle: Investigate village depopulation through the Uttarakhand case study while distinguishing permanent uninhabited status from seasonal and other migration.
research_status: editorial research dossier; source pages still require human inspection before publication
one_line_thesis: Village depopulation is not explained by one cause; the available Uttarakhand evidence points to interacting livelihood, service-access, agricultural and geographic pressures, while migration can also create opportunities.

timeline.event: Census of India records 43,324 uninhabited villages nationally and 1,048 in Uttarakhand.
Lok Sabha reply publishes state-wise Census 2011 uninhabited-village counts and describes seasonal migration in snow-bound border areas.
Uttarakhand Migration Commission survey reports 734 villages that became uninhabited after Census 2011.
PLFS annual report provides national migration estimates and patterns; these are not a count of permanently abandoned villages.
Research report discusses Uttarakhand migration drivers, service gaps and agricultural pressures using Migration Commission data.

conflicts.issue: National uninhabited-village count versus migration estimates
conflicts.version_b: PLFS migration rates measure migration during a survey reference period and do not count permanently abandoned villages.
conflicts.editorial_resolution: Keep these indicators separate and label their dates and definitions.

conflicts.version_a: Some snow-bound border villages experience seasonal winter migration.
conflicts.version_b: The 2018 Migration Commission survey reports villages that became uninhabited after 2011.
conflicts.editorial_resolution: Do not call a seasonally empty settlement permanently abandoned.

counter_arguments: Migration can improve access to employment, education, healthcare and income; it is not automatically a failure.
Some migration is seasonal or circular, and many migration streams are rural-to-rural rather than village-to-city.
Not every village must return to its historical population; policy should prioritise meaningful choices, essential services and sustainable livelihoods.

expert_perspectives.stance: Its survey data, as reproduced in the research report, identifies livelihood and employment as the leading reported migration reason.

expert_perspectives.stance: PLFS provides a broader national picture of migration and helps prevent equating all migration with village abandonment.
